newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan wants to decide on NTT issue soon -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Japan wants to decide on NTT issue soon -- minister.

text.p: Posts and Telecommunications Minister Hisao Horinouchi said on Friday that the government hopes to reach a decision soon on whether to break up Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).
"We hope to come up with a conclusion as soon as possible," Horinouchi told a news conference.

"Because the matter should be discussed by the three (political) parties, it would be too late if a decision is made by the end of this year... it should come by the end of next week or the following week," Horinouchi said.

Japan's current minority government of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) is backed by two other parties, the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake Party, which until October 20 general elections ruled with the LDP in a coalition.
Early this year, the government decided to submit a bill on the management status of NTT to parliament next January, but there had been speculation that the submission could be delayed.
The Posts and Telecommunications Ministry recommended a break-up of NTT in February 1996.
